verses.zh: 西底家登基的时候年二十一岁，在耶路撒冷作王十一年。他母亲名叫哈慕他，是立拿人耶利米的女儿。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem[NOTE:2] for 11 years. His mother’s name was Hamutal[NOTE:3] daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
notes: This final chapter does not mention Jeremiah, but its description of the downfall of Jerusalem and exile of the people validates the prophet’s ministry.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Some textual witnesses support the Kethib (consonantal text) in reading “Hamital.”
verses.commentary:
52:1-3 This information is also found in 2 Kgs. 24:18-20 and 2 Chr. 36:11-21. Zedekiah
reigned from 597 B.C. ‒ 586 B.C.

Zedekiah succeeded Jehoiachin who was exiled by Nebuchadnezzar II after only three
months (cf. 2 Kgs. 24:8-17). At that time Nebuchadnezzar II made his uncle, named Mattaniah, a
puppet king of Judah in his place. The uncle was given the throne name "Zedekiah." He was
the youngest of the children of Josiah to reign (i.e. Jehoahaz, exiled by Pharaoh Necho and
Jehoiakim, cf. 1 Chr. 3:15). He was a spiritually weak and easily manipulated person, as the
writings of Jeremiah clearly show.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM

52:1 "Hamutal" The meaning of the name is uncertain (BDB 327, KB 326). She was the
wife of King Josiah and mother of

- Jehoahaz ‒ 2 Kgs. 23:31

- Zedekiah ‒ 2 Kgs. 24:18; here

verses.zh: 西底家行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，是照约雅敬一切所行的。
verses.en: He did what displeased the Lord[NOTE:1] just as Jehoiakim had done.
notes: Heb “what was evil in the eyes of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
52:2 "he did evil in the sight of the Lord" Jeremiah uses the word "evil" (BDB 948) more
than any other OT author. This phrase became a standard evaluation of all the kings of Israel
and most of the kings of Judah. Moses had given the covenant people a clear choice (i.e. good or
evil, obedience or disobedience, prosperity or judgment, cf. Deut. 30:15,19). They said they would
choose "good" (cf. Josh. 24:16-28) but they could not/did not.

- did not seek YHWH ‒ 2 Chr. 12:14 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord)

- did not keep the covenant ‒ Deut. 31:29

- made and worshiped pagan gods ‒ Deut. 4:25; Jdg. 2:11; 3:7,12; 4:1; 6:1; 10:6; 13:1;
1 Kgs. 14:22; 15:26,34; 16:19,25,30; 22:52; 2 Kgs. 3:2; 8:18,27; 13:2,11; 14:24; 15:9,18,24,28;
17:2,17; 21:2,16,20: 23:32,37; 24:19.

- all disobedience is viewed as "doing evil" (cf. 1 Sam. 15:19) but obedience brings
acceptance (cf. 2 Chr 19:3; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

verses.zh: 因此耶和华的怒气在耶路撒冷和犹大发作，以致将人民从自己的面前赶出。
verses.en: What follows is a record of what happened to Jerusalem and Judah because of the Lord’s anger when he drove them out of his sight.[NOTE:1] Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
notes: Heb “Surely (or “for”) because of the anger of the Lord this happened in Jerusalem and Judah until he drove them out from upon his face.” For the phrase “drive out of his sight,” see 7:15.
verses.commentary:
52:3 YHWH is the God of love and acceptance. He wants all humans made in His
image to know Him (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)
but when His overtures of covenant revelation are rejected or compromised, wrath is the response.

In this text it is expressed by the powerful phrase "He cast them out from His presence"
(cf. Jer. 7:15; 2 Kgs. 13:23; 17:20; 24:20; Ps. 51:11).

"His presence" is literally "face to face." This is what we as humans were
created for! Fellowship with our Creator is "the" basic need of mankind. YHWH wants to cast
away our sins (cf. Isa. 38:17; Micah 7:19), not us!

▣ "Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon" The absence of YHWH's presence
caused him to make poor choices!

verses.zh: 西底家背叛巴比伦王。他作王第九年十月初十日，巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒率领全军来攻击耶路撒冷，对城安营，四围筑垒攻城。
verses.en: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army and set up camp outside it.[NOTE:1] They built siege ramps all around it. He arrived on the tenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year that Zedekiah ruled over Judah.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “against it.”
This would have been January 15, 588 b.c. The reckoning is based on the calendar that begins the year in the spring (Nisan = March/April).
verses.commentary:
52:4 The date of the beginning of the siege of Jerusalem is very specific (as is the date of
the fall of the city, Jer. 52:5-7).

verses.zh: 于是城被围困直到西底家王十一年。
verses.en: The city remained under siege until Zedekiah’s eleventh year.

verses.zh: 四月初九日，城里有大饥荒，甚至百姓都没有粮食。
verses.en: By the ninth day of the fourth month[NOTE:1] the famine in the city was so severe the residents[NOTE:2] had no food.
notes: According to modern reckoning that would have been July 18, 586 b.c. The siege thus lasted almost a full eighteen months.
Heb “the people of the land.”

verses.zh: 城被攻破，一切兵丁就在夜间从靠近王园两城中间的门，出城逃跑；迦勒底人正在四围攻城。他们就往亚拉巴逃去。
verses.en: They broke through the city walls, and all the soldiers tried to escape. They left the city during the night. They went through the gate between the two walls that is near the king’s garden.[NOTE:1] (The Babylonians had the city surrounded.) Then they headed for the rift valley.[NOTE:2]
notes: The king’s garden is mentioned again in Neh 3:15 in conjunction with the pool of Siloam and the stairs that go down from the City of David. This would have been in the southern part of the city near the Tyropean Valley, which agrees with the reference to the “two walls,” which were probably the walls on the eastern and western hills.

The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) extends from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba. In this context the portion that they head to is the Jordan Valley near Jericho, intending to escape across the river to Moab or Ammon. It appears from 40:14 and 41:15 that the Ammonites were known to harbor fugitives from the Babylonians.
verses.commentary:
52:7 "the city was broken into" Although it does not state specifically how, the implication is
that the siege machines broke down a gate or a piece of the outer wall (i.e. probably the north wall).

A siege machine was a portable "A-frame" with ropes, suspending a large log. This
was placed next to the outer wall where it repeatedly rammed the bottom building blocks which destablized the whole wall.

▣ "between the two walls" Many ancient cities had double outer walls (i.e. Jericho). The
space between them was designed to be a "killing zone," but here this space provided a way of escape
when the wall was breached in another part of the city.

▣ "the Arabah" This refers to the Jordan Rift Valley, which extends from the area of the
Sea of Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba (cf. 2 Sam. 4:7). It was lower than the surrounding area and during this period
had dense forest and vegetation. South of the Dead Sea (cf. Deut. 2:8) it would be the large wilderness depression
going south/southwest.

verses.zh: 迦勒底的军队追赶西底家王，在耶利哥的平原追上他。他的全军都离开他四散了。
verses.en: But the Babylonian army chased after the king. They caught up with Zedekiah in the plains[NOTE:1] of Jericho,[NOTE:2] and his entire army deserted him.
notes: See the note at Jer 39:5.
For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
verses.commentary:
52:8-11 This is a summary of what happened to Judah's royalty.

- Zedekiah was captured as he fled the city, Jer. 52:8

- Zedekiah was brought north to Nebuchadnezzar's camp in Riblah in the land of
Hamath, for a face-to-face meeting, Jer. 52:9

- Nebuchadnezzar killed Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, Jer. 52:10

- he also killed Zedekiah's officials and generals (lit. "princes"), Jer. 52:10

- he blinded Zedekiah, Jer. 52:11

- he exiled him and put him in prison until his death in Babylon, Jer. 52:11

verses.zh: 迦勒底人就拿住王，带他到在哈马地利比拉的巴比伦王那里；巴比伦王便审判他。
verses.en: They captured him and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah[NOTE:1] in the territory of Hamath, and he passed sentence on him there.
notes: Riblah was a strategic town on the Orontes River in Syria. It was at a crossing of the major roads between Egypt and Mesopotamia. Pharaoh Necho had earlier received Jehoahaz there and put him in chains (2 Kgs 23:33) prior to taking him captive to Egypt. Nebuchadnezzar had set up his base camp for conducting his campaigns against the Palestinian states there and was now sitting in judgment on prisoners brought to him.

verses.zh: 巴比伦王在西底家眼前杀了他的众子，又在利比拉杀了犹大的一切首领，
verses.en: The king of Babylon had Zedekiah’s sons put to death while Zedekiah was forced to watch. He also had all the nobles of Judah put to death there at Riblah.

verses.zh: 并且剜了西底家的眼睛，用铜链锁着他，带到巴比伦去，将他囚在监里，直到他死的日子。
verses.en: He had Zedekiah’s eyes put out and had him bound in chains.[NOTE:1] Then the king of Babylon had him led off to Babylon, and he was imprisoned there until the day he died.
notes: Heb “fetters of bronze.” The more generic “chains” is used in the translation because “fetters” is a word unfamiliar to most modern readers.

verses.zh: 巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒十九年五月初十日，在巴比伦王面前侍立的护卫长尼布撒拉旦进入耶路撒冷，
verses.en: On the tenth[NOTE:1] day of the fifth month,[NOTE:2] in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the royal guard[NOTE:3] who served[NOTE:4] the king of Babylon, arrived in Jerusalem.
notes: The parallel account in 2 Kgs 25:8 has “seventh.”
The tenth day of the month would have been August 17, 586 b.c. in modern reckoning.
For the meaning of this phrase see BDB 371 s.v. טַבָּח 2 and compare the usage in Gen 39:1.
Heb “stood before.”
verses.commentary:
52:12 As the date of the siege and the fall of Jerusalem are specified, so too, the date
when Nebuchadnezzar's military official arrived in Jerusalem to oversee its destruction.

- burned the temple, Jer. 52:13

- burned the palace, Jer. 52:13

- burned all large houses, Jer. 52:13

- broke down the whole outer wall, Jer. 52:14

- exiled even more people

- left a few people, Jer. 52:15

- defectors from the Neo-Babylonian military

- the remaining craftsmen

The parallel in 2 Kgs. 25:8 has "the seventh day," not the "tenth day." R. K. Harrison,
Tyndale OT Commentary Series, p. 190, speculates the difference is between the day Nebuzaradan
came to Jerusalem and the day the destruction started. This follows a rabbinical tradition
(B. Ta'anit 29a). The NASB Study Bible, (p. 1143) asserts that one of the two dates
(i.e. "seven" or "ten") is a copyist error.

In the ANE there were two ways to calculate a king's reign:

- from the first partial year

- from the annual coronation ceremony

Often these ways are mixed, as is done in Jer. 52:12 (1 above) and Jer. 52:19 (2 above).

verses.zh: 用火焚烧耶和华的殿和王宫，又焚烧耶路撒冷的房屋，就是各大户家的房屋。
verses.en: He burned down the Lord’s temple, the royal palace, and all the houses in Jerusalem, including every large house.

verses.zh: 跟从护卫长迦勒底的全军就拆毁耶路撒冷四围的城墙。
verses.en: The whole Babylonian army that came with the captain of the royal guard tore down the walls that surrounded Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 那时护卫长尼布撒拉旦将民中最穷的和城里所剩下的百姓，并已经投降巴比伦王的人，以及大众所剩下的人，都掳去了。
verses.en: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the royal guard, took into exile some of the poor,[NOTE:1] the rest of the people who remained in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen.
notes: Heb “poor of the people.”

verses.zh: 但护卫长尼布撒拉旦留下些民中最穷的，使他们修理葡萄园，耕种田地。
verses.en: But he[NOTE:1] left behind some of the poor[NOTE:2] and gave them fields and vineyards.
notes: Heb “Nebuzaradan, the captain of the royal guard.” However, the subject is clear from the preceding, and modern English style would normally avoid repeating the proper name and title.
Heb “poor of the land.”

verses.zh: 耶和华殿的铜柱并殿内的盆座和铜海，迦勒底人都打碎了，将那铜运到巴比伦去了，
verses.en: The Babylonians broke the two bronze pillars in the temple of the Lord, as well as the movable stands and the large bronze basin called “The Sea.”[NOTE:1] They took all the bronze to Babylon.
notes: For discussion of the items listed here, see the study notes at Jer 27:19.
verses.commentary:
52:17-23 This is a list of the things taken to Babylon.

- the bronze pillars of the temple (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PILLARS)

- the stands (i.e. twelve bronze bulls, Jer. 52:20) and the bronze sea (cf. Jer. 52:20-23)

- pots, shovels, snuffers, basins, pans, and all other bronze vessels used in the temple

- bowls, firepans, basins, pots, the lampstand, its spoons, libation bowls, all gold and silver items

Jeremiah 52:17-18 lists bronze items, while Jer. 52:19 lists gold and silver items. Verses 20-23
describe in detail the two bronze pillars (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:40-42).

verses.zh: 又带去锅、铲子、蜡剪、盘子、调羹，并所用的一切铜器、
verses.en: They also took the pots, shovels,[NOTE:1] trimming shears,[NOTE:2] basins, pans, and all the bronze utensils used by the priests.[NOTE:3]
notes: These shovels were used to clean the altar.
These trimming shears were used to trim the wicks of the lamps.
Heb “with which they served (or “fulfilled their duty”).”

verses.zh: 杯、火鼎、碗、盆、灯台、调羹、爵，无论金的银的，护卫长也都带去了。
verses.en: The captain of the royal guard took the gold and silver bowls, censers,[NOTE:1] basins, pots, lampstands, pans, and vessels.[NOTE:2]
notes: The censers held the embers used for the incense offerings.
These vessels were used for drink offerings.

verses.zh: 所罗门为耶和华殿所造的两根铜柱、一个铜海，并座下的十二只铜牛，这一切的铜多得无法可称。
verses.en: The bronze of the items that King Solomon made for the Lord’s temple (including the two pillars, the large bronze basin called “The Sea,” the 12 bronze bulls under “The Sea,” and the movable stands[NOTE:1]) was too heavy to be weighed.
notes: The translation follows the LXX (Greek version), which reflects the description in 1 Kgs 7:25-26. The Hebrew text reads, “the 12 bronze bulls under the movable stands.” הַיָּם (hayyam, “The Sea”) has been accidentally omitted by homoioarcton; note that the following form, הַמְּכֹנוֹת (hammekhonot, “the movable stands”), also begins with the article.

verses.zh: 这一根柱子高十八肘，厚四指，是空的，围十二肘。
verses.en: Each of the pillars was about 27 feet[NOTE:1] high, about 18 feet[NOTE:2] in circumference, three inches[NOTE:3] thick, and hollow.
notes: Heb “18 cubits.” A “cubit” was a unit of measure, approximately equivalent to a foot and a half.
Heb “12 cubits.” A “cubit” was a unit of measure, approximately equivalent to a foot and a half.
Heb “four fingers.”

verses.zh: 柱上有铜顶，高五肘；铜顶的周围有网子和石榴，都是铜的。那一根柱子照此一样，也有石榴。
verses.en: The bronze top of one pillar was about 7½ feet[NOTE:1] high and had bronze latticework and pomegranate-shaped ornaments all around it. The second pillar with its pomegranate-shaped ornaments was like it.
notes: Heb “5 cubits.” A “cubit” was a unit of measure, approximately equivalent to a foot and a half.

verses.zh: 柱子四面有九十六个石榴，在网子周围，共有一百石榴。
verses.en: There were 96 pomegranate-shaped ornaments on the sides; in all there were 100 pomegranate-shaped ornaments over the latticework that went around it.

verses.zh: 护卫长拿住大祭司西莱雅、副祭司西番亚，和三个把门的，
verses.en: The captain of the royal guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest who was second in rank, and the three doorkeepers.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note at Jer 35:4.
verses.commentary:
52:24 As Zedekiah was forced to view the death of his "sons" and "princes," so now the
temple leadership was forced to view the exile of the temple treasures and decorations.

- Seraiah the high priest (see genealogy in 1 Chr. 6:1-15)

- Zephaniah the second priest (cf. Jer. 29:24-32; 37:3)

verses.zh: 又从城中拿住一个管理兵丁的官（或译：太监），并在城里所遇常见王面的七个人和检点国民军长的书记，以及城里所遇见的国民六十个人。
verses.en: From the city he took an official who was in charge of the soldiers, seven of the king’s advisers who were discovered in the city, an official army secretary who drafted citizens[NOTE:1] for military service, and 60 citizens who were discovered in the middle of the city.
notes: Heb “men, from the people of the land” (also later in this verse).
verses.commentary:
52:25 Others were also brought to Nebuchadnezzar II at Riblah.

- the city official who was overseer of the Judean military

- seven of Zedekiah's advisors

- the scribe of the commander of enlistment for the Judean military

- sixty citizens of Jerusalem (probably of the wealthy land owner class)

verses.zh: 护卫长尼布撒拉旦将这些人带到利比拉的巴比伦王那里。
verses.en: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the royal guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.commentary: 52:26-27 All of these mentioned above were killed at Riblah and all others were taken into exile.

verses.zh: 巴比伦王就把他们击杀在哈马地的利比拉。这样，犹大人被掳去离开本地。
verses.en: The king of Babylon ordered them to be executed[NOTE:1] at Riblah in the territory of Hamath.So Judah was taken into exile away from its land.
notes: Heb “struck them down and killed them.”

verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒所掳的民数记在下面：在他第七年掳去犹大人三千零二十三名；
verses.en: Here is the official record of the number of people[NOTE:1] Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: In the seventh year,[NOTE:2] 3,023 Jews;
notes: Heb “these are the people.”
This would be 597 b.c.
verses.commentary:
52:28-30 These verses list the different groups, numbers, and the dates they were
exiled. Remember the city of Jerusalem was partially captured in 605, 597, mostly in 586, and completely
in 582 B.C. The current event was 586 B.C. Earlier events
were 605 and 597 B.C. A later event was after the murder of Gedaliah
(582 B.C.). This account may have been written before or after 582 B.C.,
but the "twenty-third year" of Jer. 52:30 fits 582 B.C., if one calculates from
605 B.C. The total number of people exiled in this list is 4,600.

These verses are absent in the LXX. The numbers also differ from the book of Kings account. These
historical records of Kings and Jeremiah are very similar but not exact. Both apparently used the same
Hebrew source document (cf. Tyndale OT Series, p. 190). Possibly Jeremiah 52 lists only the adult males.

verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒十八年从耶路撒冷掳去八百三十二人；
verses.en: in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year,[NOTE:1] 832 people from Jerusalem;
notes: This would be 586 b.c.

verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒二十三年，护卫长尼布撒拉旦掳去犹大人七百四十五名；共有四千六百人。
verses.en: in Nebuchadnezzar’s twenty-third year,[NOTE:1] Nebuzaradan, the captain of the royal guard, carried into exile 745 Judeans. In all, 4,600 people went into exile.
notes: This would be 581 b.c.

verses.zh: 犹大王约雅斤被掳后三十七年，巴比伦王以未米罗达元年十二月二十五日，使犹大王约雅斤抬头，提他出监，
verses.en: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of King Jehoiachin of Judah, on the twenty-fifth[NOTE:1] day of the twelfth month,[NOTE:2] King Evil Merodach of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, pardoned[NOTE:3] King Jehoiachin of Judah and released him from prison.
notes: The parallel account in 2 Kgs 25:27 has “twenty-seventh.”
The twenty-fifth day would be March 20, 561 b.c. in modern reckoning.
Heb “lifted up the head of.”
verses.commentary:
52:31-34 This paragraph describes the later, favorable treatment of King Jehoiachin, who
was exiled by Nebuchadnezzar II after he had reigned only three months (he was considered by the Jews
to be the legitimate heir of Josiah), by Evil-merodack (or Amel-Marduk), who reigned from
562-560 B.C. (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:27-30). One wonders what theological purpose this
last paragraph serves.

- further historical detail

- a sign of future hope of release from exile

- a way to show YHWH still had a hand in Judah's destiny

- ending the prophecy of Jeremiah in a positive way

verses.zh: 又对他说恩言，使他的位高过与他一同在巴比伦众王的位，
verses.en: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a more prestigious position than[NOTE:1] the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
notes: Heb “made his throne above the throne of.”

verses.zh: 给他脱了囚服。他终身在巴比伦王面前吃饭。
verses.en: Jehoiachin[NOTE:1] took off his prison clothes and ate daily in the king’s presence for the rest of his life.
notes: The subject is unstated in the Hebrew text, but Jehoiachin is clearly the subject of the following verb.

verses.zh: 巴比伦王赐他所需用的食物，日日赐他一分，终身是这样，直到他死的日子。
verses.en: He was given daily provisions by the king of Babylon for the rest of his life until the day he died.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- There are three historical events discussed in this historical appendage.

- the fall of the city of Jerusalem, Jer. 52:1-11 (cf. Jer. 39:1-10)

- the destruction of the city and its temple, Jer. 52:12-23

- a summary statement of the several deportations of Judeans to Babylon, Jer. 52:23-34

- This chapter contains the same basic information as 2 Kings 24:10-25:30. Comparing these
two recordings of the same event shows modern readers something of scribal tendencies.

This same event is discussed in Jeremiah 39, however, this chapter is
much closer to the 2 Kings account, which implies that it was added by an editor and not
written by Jeremiah. The NASB Study Bible (p. 1143) says that Baruch may have been the
author of this chapter and that both the author of Kings and this chapter may have used a
common source.

- All that Jeremiah said would happen, occurred. He was a true prophet (cf. Deuteronomy 13, 18).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: JEREMIAH 52:1-11

1Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven
years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. 2He did evil in the sight
of the Lord like all that Jehoiakim had done. 3For through the anger of the
Lord this came about in Jerusalem and Judah until He cast them out from His presence. And
Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. 4Now it came about in the ninth year of his reign, on the tenth day
of the tenth month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, camped against it and built a
siege wall all around it. 5So the city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah. 6On the ninth
day of the fourth month the famine was so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land. 7Then
the city was broken into, and all the men of war fled and went forth from the city at night by way of the gate between the two walls which
was by the king's garden, though the Chaldeans were all around the city. And they went by way of the Arabah. 8But
the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
9Then they captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed
sentence on him. 10The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also slaughtered all the
princes of Judah in Riblah. 11Then he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him with bronze fetters
and brought him to Babylon and put him in prison until the day of his death.
